claim: E1: Rogers supplies five perceived innovation attributes and adopter categories based on relative timing.
source_or_reference: Rogers, Diffusion of Innovations, fifth edition, publisher excerpt. https://www.simonandschuster.com/books/Diffusion-of-Innovations-5th-Edition/Everett-M-Rogers/9780743222099
notes: Conceptual framework; no current RAG prevalence data.

claim: E2: The original RAG study combines retrieved external memory with generation and evaluates knowledge-intensive tasks.
source_or_reference: Lewis et al., Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks. https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401
notes: Technical origin and mechanism; benchmark results are not adoption evidence.

claim: E3: Morgan Stanley reported 98% adoption of its Assistant among its Financial Advisor teams.
date_or_recency: Published and reported as of 2024-06-26; accessed 2026-10-23.
notes: Single firm and within-firm team denominator; adjacent knowledge-assistant application. This release does not establish exact RAG architecture, usage frequency, or sector penetration. Historical.

claim: E4: 75% of 118 responding firms reported AI use in the 2024 Bank of England/FCA survey.
source_or_reference: Bank of England/FCA, Artificial intelligence in UK financial services 2024. https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/report/2024/artificial-intelligence-in-uk-financial-services-2024
notes: UK financial-services respondents; broad AI definition, not RAG or investment-research assistants. Respondent proportion is not a representative estimate for unspecified midsize peers. Historical.

claim: E5: A July 2026 UK adoption plan explicitly identifies its cited 75% figure as findings published in 2024.
source_or_reference: Financial Services AI Adoption Plan, published by HM Treasury. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/ai-adoption-plan-financial-services/financial-services-ai-adoption-plan
date_or_recency: Published 2026-07-14; underlying cited AI statistic 2024; accessed 2026-10-23.
notes: Fresh publication is not fresh measurement. Supports recency caution, not a new RAG adoption estimate.

claim: E6: An AWS article co-written with Nippon Life India Asset Management describes an adopted RAG solution and retrieval/parsing challenges.
source_or_reference: Shivakumar and Pandey, Nippon India Mutual Fund RAG implementation. https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/how-nippon-india-mutual-fund-improved-the-accuracy-of-ai-assistant-responses-using-advanced-rag-methods-on-amazon-bedrock/
date_or_recency: Published 2025-07-29; deployment observation date not separately specified; accessed 2026-10-23.
evidence_type: Vendor and adopter co-authored implementation account
notes: Named Indian asset manager; explicit RAG, selected case, commercial interest; no peer denominator or independent performance audit. Over 12 months old; refresh before rollout timing.
